overall_assessment: Anonymization works well for UiA. In all 28 courses the course-coordinator names are removed, both the 'Emneansvarlig: Name' form on one line and the label with the name on the next line, and multi-name 'Emneansvarlige:' blocks. The '(Høst YYYY)' and '(Høst 2022–Vår 2023)' title stamps, the FS timestamp, the faculty e-mail and an English 'Contact persons:' block with personal e-mails are also removed. No literature, subject-matter names or content years are lost. The pre-pass flags are false alarms: 'name_like' matches philosophers (Kierkegaard, Sartre, Buber, McLuhan), course and programme titles, and 'removed' matches short pages that are mostly header. The only leftover is one course-run date in an 'Annen informasjon' note.

findings.description: A date when the course runs is left in the plan. It is scheduling for one offering, like the exam dates the generic rules already remove, not course content. The format is a day range followed by an English month, a comma and the year, which no date rule matches. Only 1 of 28 courses in the sample has it, so the impact is cosmetic.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: In R/anonymize.R, .long_date_regex expects 'dd[.] month' followed by a year without a comma, and it allows no day range ('17 - 21'). .approval_date_regex also needs an approval verb before the date, so a run date in prose survives.
findings.suggested_fix: Low priority. Either add to .anon_uia() a removal for '(?i)\b(?:is|will be) offered\s+\d{1,2}(?:\s*[-–]\s*\d{1,2})?\.?\s+<month>,?\s+\d{4}' that keeps the sentence stem, or make .long_dates_regex accept an optional day range and a comma before the year (keep the .not_gov_rule guard). Add a test case 'offered 17 - 21 March, 2025' in tests/testthat/test-anonymize.R.
